_readme: Recorded highlight/analysis channels for the 'Videos' tab (see js/videos.js). Unlike streams.json, this section is NOT gated behind a live basho — it shows all the time.
Each entry: { "id", "label", "channelUrl", "channelId", "disabled", "note" }. 'id' just needs to be unique in this file.
'channelUrl' is the plain https://www.youtube.com/@handle URL — always required, used both as the 'open channel' link and as the fallback card when there's no embed.

'channelId' is YouTube's UC... internal channel ID — optional. When present, the card embeds that channel's uploads playlist (https://www.youtube.com/embed/videoseries?list=UU...), which auto-updates as the channel posts new videos, so there's nothing to maintain. Get it by opening the channel and viewing this app's own note in js/videos.js for the lookup method, or a lookup tool such as https://commentpicker.com/youtube-channel-id.php. It always starts with 'UC' — js/videos.js swaps that prefix for 'UU' itself to get the uploads playlist, don't do that substitution here.

Set "disabled": true to keep an entry out of the rendered grid without deleting it — e.g. while you're still tracking down its channelId, or if a channel has gone quiet. 'note' is optional free text shown nowhere in the UI; it's just for your own records in this file (e.g. why something is disabled).

The entries below were checked while building this feature (see the channel's own 'About' page / RSS feed for the channelId, e.g. view-source on https://www.youtube.com/@handle and search 'channelId', or https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=UC... once you have a guess). Channel URLs and IDs on YouTube do change hands/get deleted, so it's worth a periodic recheck — Kintamayama below is a concrete example: a former top-3 channel that no longer has a working YouTube presence at all.
Ranking/description text in 'label' is loosely based on community round-ups (r/Sumo, watch guides) circa mid-2026 — treat it as a starting point, not gospel.

videos.label: Sumo Prime Time (official JSA English-language show)
Kintamayama
videos.note: Kintamayama's original YouTube channel was taken down in the January 2023 mass takedown, and a follow-up channel was also deleted; he moved to Rumble for a while (https://rumble.com/user/Kintamayama). This channel now displays as 'Mordy Dunchy' with no sumo content in its About section, but the site owner confirmed directly that this is the same, rebranded channel/handle (@knitamaya) — worth bearing in mind if the channel's public branding changes again.
